title: Region
description: A region within a country (real ISO 3166-2 subdivision) or, for countries without subdivisions, the single synthetic whole-country entry with code 'WHOLE'.

code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (e.g. FR-BRE) when the parent country has real subdivisions, otherwise the literal 'WHOLE'.

local.description: The region's name in the language(s) actually local to it — not necessarily every official language of the parent country. E.g. CH-ZH (German-speaking) has one entry (deu); the CHE WHOLE fallback, representing the whole multilingual country, has all four (deu/fra/ita/roh). Mirrors country.schema.json's name.local[] shape for the same reason: some regions (federal-country subdivisions especially) can legitimately have more than one locally-used name.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-3 code, e.g. fra, deu, tah

climates.description: Köppen climate classes present in this region, with a short description.

prideOf.description: What locals are most proud of.

seasonCalendar.description: Maps each non-'allYear' season label used anywhere in this file's entertainment/traditionalDishes/traditionalClothing to the calendar month(s) it covers HERE — this is what makes 'what season is it right now in this region' computable from today's date (see usage_examples/python/get_data_by_ip.py). Required (checked by scripts/validate.py, not JSON Schema alone) whenever any seasonal field in this file uses a season other than 'allYear'. Together the months[] across all entries here must partition the year exactly (each of 1-12 appears in exactly one entry) — also checked by scripts/validate.py.

season.description: Never 'allYear' — allYear content applies regardless of season and needs no calendar entry.

months.description: Calendar months (1=January .. 12=December) belonging to this season in this region. Reversed vs. the Northern-Hemisphere-typical assumption for Southern-Hemisphere regions (e.g. 'summer' = Dec-Feb there).

businessRhythm.description: Work/rest rhythm and business seasonality for this region — deliberately region-level (not country-level), because it genuinely varies by region even within one country (e.g. Paris's touristic zones have Sunday-trading exemptions the rest of France doesn't). When the underlying rule is national law, that fact belongs in the parent country.yaml's legalConstraints[] with a sourceId, and this block is just customary description/regional nuance on top of it (no source needed). But when the law genuinely varies by region — most commonly in federal countries, where e.g. shop-opening hours are the *canton's* own law, not the federal government's — this block itself can carry a sourced legal fact, via the optional sourceIds field below. Most businessRhythm content is still qualitative/customary and doesn't need a source; only add sourceIds when a specific claim here genuinely has one.

restDays.description: Which weekdays are widely treated as non-working days here.

notableShutdownPeriods.description: Recurring periods when business activity noticeably slows/stops (e.g. August in much of France/Italy).

notes.description: Region-specific nuance/exceptions to the country's general legal picture, e.g. a touristic-zone trading exemption.

sourceIds.description: Optional. Set this when notes/restDays/typicalWorkHours/lunchBreakTiming state a specific, sourceable legal or factual claim (e.g. a canton's own trading-hours law) rather than general customary description — an array, not a single value, because a region's businessRhythm text can legitimately draw on more than one source (e.g. the general closure rule plus a later amendment). Leave unset for purely qualitative/customary content, which is most businessRhythm content.

sources.description: Registry of authoritative sources backing the statistical/factual fields in this file (religions, businessRhythm.notableShutdownPeriods and businessRhythm.sourceIds when sourced). Every sourceId used below must have a matching entry here — checked by scripts/validate.py, not by JSON Schema alone.

id.description: Unique within this file. Referenced by sourceId fields elsewhere in the same file.

publisher.description: The authoritative body, e.g. a national statistics office.

year.description: Year the underlying data refers to (not necessarily the access date).

accessedDate.description: Date this source was consulted, YYYY-MM-DD.

note.description: Exactly what in this file was taken from this source.

sourceIdRef.description: Must match a sources[].id declared in this same file.

seasonalList.description: Grouped by season. A closed enum rather than free text, so consumers can reliably filter by the visitor's current season — but it deliberately covers more than the four-season model: tropical/equatorial regions use dry/wet instead of spring/summer/autumn/winter (see PYF), and regions without meaningful seasonality use a single 'allYear' entry. Note: 'summer'/'winter' etc. are calendar-month-agnostic labels — this schema does not encode which months they cover or reconcile Southern-Hemisphere season timing against Northern-Hemisphere labels; a consumer mapping 'current date' to 'current season' must handle that itself (e.g. via the country/region's approximate latitude or climates[].koppenCode).

season.description: spring/summer/autumn/winter for temperate regions, dry/wet for tropical/equatorial regions, allYear for content with no meaningful seasonality.
